successors.name: Pagan Kingdom
successors.text: the Pyu land still outside Pagan in 1044 as Cliopatria draws it: Sri Ksetra near Pyay and the southern dry zone, and the Mu valley around Halin; the Pagan page's 1044 districts (Mandalay, Meiktila…

ledger.x: c. 180 BCE: the Pyu build Beikthano, the first walled city of the Irrawaddy dry zone. Infobox 'Beikthano founded: c. 180 BCE'; 'In about the 2nd century BCE' the Pyu entered the Irrawaddy valley; Beikthano's remains 'date from 200 BCE to 100 CE' and its walls are 'radiocarbon dated to a period between 180 BCE and 610…
70: Halin founded in the Mu valley and becomes the premier Pyu city.
638: the Vikrama dynasty of Sri Ksetra launches the Burmese calendar.
739: Duttabaung founds the second Sri Ksetra dynasty.
763: Nanzhao takes the upper Irrawaddy valley.
835: the last recorded Nanzhao attack at Halin.
960: the Burmans lead the dry zone.
1044: Anawrahta comes to power at Pagan; the Pyu cities pass under Pagan.

wars.name: Nanzhao invasions of the Pyu (832–835)
wars.outcome: Halin destroyed and 3,000 prisoners taken in 832; 'in 835, they subdued Michen (near the mouth of the Ayeyarwady River in lower Burma)' and 'returned to Halin in 835 and carried off many prisoners'.

certainty.note: A network of walled cities with no recorded frontier; the outer limit is the Irrawaddy dry zone from Halin to Sri Ksetra.
